name: Afro House
sources: style-research-extended vol.4 house — Black Coffee (the Afro-house archetype, 115–125 straight, backbeat on 2&4)
style-research-extended vol.4 house — Organic / Afro house: 118–125 for the club form
style-research-extended vol.4 amapiano — finding 7: the identity test is categorical, and Black Coffee STAYS in `house`
style-research-extended vol.4 afrobeats — Niniola (the Lagos Afro-house wing: four-on-floor, clap on 2&4, open hat on all offbeat 8ths, shaker 16ths)
notes: House's four-on-the-floor with an African percussion ensemble on top of it, at a tempo below the house norm. ⛔⛔ **This archetype exists because volume 4 refused to fake it.** The amapiano researcher settled the boundary with a categorical test — Splice's *"without the log drum, it's not amapiano"* — plus two numbers: a clap on 2 & 4 immediately reads as house, and amapiano centres at 113 against Afro-house's 118. The recommendation was explicit: **Black Coffee stays in `house` and does not move**, and the wider cohort (DJ Zinhle, Bucie, Msaki, Keinemusik) *"is owed a future `afro-house` model rather than this one"*. This is that model, and it is authored so those names have somewhere true to go — ⚠ **nothing was moved into it here.** Reassigning artists is its own change with its own gates. ⛔ **The percussion ensemble is the archetype, and it is the one thing the engine can actually carry.** The research describes layered congas, djembe, shakers and hand claps programmed as **2-bar polyrhythmic figures rather than 1-bar loops**, with continuous velocity variation. `percs.densityPerBar` is [5, 10] against `house`'s [1, 3] and `placement` is `any` rather than `offbeat`, because an ensemble that only ever answers the offbeat is a shaker, not an ensemble. The 2-bar figure itself is **not** expressible — the perc scheduler places per bar — and pretending otherwise by inventing a key would be a knob nothing reads. `humanize.velocityVar` at 0.26 is the highest on the roster's house family, which is the closest this engine comes to *"continuous velocity variation"*. ⚠ **The backbeat is present and soft.** `snare.placement` is `backbeat_24` — the parameter that makes this read as house rather than as amapiano — with `transient: "soft"` and a low ghost probability, because the research says the clap *"is present but soft"*. The open hat is on the offbeat 8ths and **understated**: `prob` 0.55 against `house`'s 0.92, and one or two a bar against house's two to four. ⚠ **The low end is the 808 lane, and that is this engine's house-family answer rather than a shortcut.** `bass::generate` returns an empty lane whenever `drums.bass808.role` is `bassline` — `house` and `amapiano` both inherit exactly that — so authoring a separate `bassline` block here would be a block nothing reads. The 808 is authored instead: `sustain: "legato"` for the *"deep rounded sub, long notes"* the research names, `slideProb` at 0.05 because it *"moves with the chord roots"* rather than sliding, and no distortion. ⚠ **Harmony avoids cadences on purpose.** *"Long sustained single-chord sections"* and a two-chord `i–VI` movement, m9 and m11 colour, *"the harmony is a bed for percussion and voice"* — so `vamp` and `2_bars_per_chord` carry the weight, `chordDurationBeats` reaches 16, and the seventh/ninth share is the highest of the three neighbours. ⚠ **The fill lane is the snare, and it was `perc` for one round.** `fills.lane: "perc"` is authorable and `every_shipped_genre_fills_at_the_cycle_it_authors` counts roll-articulated notes on **Snare and Clap only** — so the model filled on its authored cycle and the gate saw an empty bar 4. A percussion-led fill is not a thing this engine measures, and inventing one here would have been a claim nothing checks. ⚠ **INFERRED, hence `medium`.** Sourced: the tempo band and its centre, the four-on-floor, the clap on 2&4, the offbeat open hat, the shaker 16ths, the percussion ensemble and its polyrhythm, the sub's shape, the instrument list and the long-form arrangement. Inferred: every velocity tier, every register, `swing` at 0.52 (between house's straight 0.50 and amapiano's 0.58 — the research describes a cross-rhythm in the percussion, not a swung grid), the `intervals`/`contour` split and the mode names. ⚠ **What this model cannot say:** the vocals in South African languages that the research calls a defining feature are a topline, and this engine writes no vocal; the 6–9 minute long form lives in `arrangement.sectionBars` as 16- and 32-bar blocks, which is as much of it as a four- or eight-bar loop can hold.
